title: Baked Potato, Peel Eaten, with Sour Cream

content.title: About
content.content: Baked potato is one of the most popular ways to prepare this tuber. Keeping the skin on retains most of the nutrients, and sour cream adds a smooth, creamy flavor while boosting the dish’s nutritional profile.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The potato skin contains more fiber, vitamin C, B6, and potassium than the flesh.
Serving baked potatoes with sour cream is a long‑standing tradition in Russia, Ukraine, and other Eastern European countries.
Sour cream, made from fermented cream, is rich in vitamins A and D and beneficial fatty acids.
Baked potatoes can be prepared in an oven, microwave, or over an open fire.
Potatoes are among the cheapest and most widely available sources of carbohydrates worldwide.

items.title: High in Fiber
items.content: The skin provides a substantial amount of dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Vitamin C Source
items.content: Vitamin C in the skin helps strengthen the immune system and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Heart Support
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure, contributing to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Probiotic Benefits
items.content: Sour cream contains live bacterial cultures that can improve gut microbiota.

items.title: Energy Supply
items.content: Carbohydrates in the potato quickly replenish glycogen stores, useful for athletes and active individuals.

items.title: High Glycemic Index
items.content: Baked potatoes can raise blood sugar rapidly, which is important for people with diabetes to monitor.

items.title: Dairy Allergy
items.content: Sour cream may trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Sodium Content
items.content: Sour cream is often salted; excessive sodium intake can increase blood pressure.

items.title: Green Spots Toxicity
items.content: If the potato has green areas, it may contain solanine, a toxin that should be removed.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the baked potato hot, split it open and top with sour cream. Optional toppings include fresh dill, minced garlic, or grated cheese. The skin is eaten together with the flesh after a thorough wash.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw potatoes in a cool, dark place at 7‑10 °C. Cooked baked potatoes are best consumed within 2‑3 days, kept in the refrigerator in an airtight container.
